title: Interfacial engineering accelerates desolvation kinetics for high-performance alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries
content: Alkaline zinc–iron flow batteries (AZIFBs) are promising candidates for grid-scale energy storage owing to their high cell voltage, intrinsic safety, and compelling cost-effectiveness. Nevertheless, their high-capacity operation is limited by slow interfacial desolvation of zincate ions (Zn(OH)42−), which disrupts ion flux and promotes dendritic deposition and corrosion. Here, we report an anion-chelator-induced interfacial transport channel that accelerates Zn(OH)42− desolvation and regulates zinc deposition. Cyclooctaamylose (COA) serves as a supramolecular scaffold that weakens the Zn–OH solvation shell of incoming Zn(OH)42− and lowers the activation barriers for desolvation and charge transfer. Preferential adsorption of COA on zinc also limits hydroxide uptake, thereby suppressing corrosion and promoting compact deposits. Consequently, these interfacial effects allow AZIFBs to operate at a remarkable areal capacity of 200 mAh cm−2 (at 89% state of charge) with a high coulombic efficiency of 99.0%, while delivering stable operation for over 800 hours at a high capacity of 140 mAh cm−2. Driven by these rapid interfacial kinetics, the battery endures nearly 1200 cycles at an ultra-high current density of 200 mA cm−2 and delivers a power density of 1028 mW cm−2. These results establish targeted interfacial desolvation control as a mechanistically grounded strategy for high-capacity and high-power flow batteries.
